bib.title: MMBench: Is Your Multi-modal Model an All-around Player?

read.skipped: per-model dev/test/CN tables 10-13 skimmed (numbers not individually recorded); reference list skimmed

question: How can large vision-language models be evaluated objectively, fine-grained and robustly despite weak instruction following?
hypothesis: Circular shifted-choice evaluation plus LLM choice extraction gives a more robust, discriminative evaluation than single-pass exact matching.
contributions: Systematically-constructed dataset of 3,217 questions over 20 skills
Robust evaluation: CircularEval and GPT-4 choice matching
Analysis and observations on a series of well-known VLMs

method.summary: Builds a 3,217-question bilingual multiple-choice VLM benchmark with a 3-level, 20-ability taxonomy, quality filtering by text-only LLM majority voting and VLM all-wrong checks, a CircularEval protocol (N shifted-choice passes, all must be right) and GPT-4 choice extraction. Evaluates ~30 VLMs zero-shot on dev/test, EN and CN.

datasets.name: MMBench
datasets.split: dev:test 4:6; dev answers public, test answers on evaluation server
datasets.source: 80.5% Internet (2590), ~20% images from validation sets of public datasets (COCO 179, ScienceQA 156, ARAS 76, Places 59, etc.), questions self-built by volunteers
datasets.preprocessing: text-only filter (GPT-4, Gemini-Pro, Qwen-Max; if more than half/two correct, manual check); wrong filter (3 proprietary + InternLM-XComposer2 + LLaVA-v1.5-13B all wrong under CircularEval -> manual check)

models.name: Open-source VLMs (OpenFlamingo v2, MiniGPT-4, InstructBLIP, IDEFICS, VisualGLM, Qwen-VL-Chat, MiniCPM-V, LLaVA-v1.5, mPLUG-Owl2, CogVLM, Yi-VL, InternLM-XComposer(2), LLaVA-InternLM2 etc.)

inference.samples: CircularEval: N passes per question, N = number of choices (2-4); stops at first failed pass
inference.prompting: zero-shot, same prompt for all VLMs (Hint optional, Question, options A-D, 'Please select the correct answer from the options above.'); few-shot and CoT tried, 'no encouraging results'

parameters.choice_extraction: heuristic label match first, then gpt-4-0125 with 2 in-context examples; returns Z if no option fits

metrics.name: CircularEval Top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: question solved only if correct in all N circularly-shifted passes

metrics.name: Choice-extractor alignment with humans
metrics.definition: extracted label identical to human extraction on ~420 hard samples

eval.protocol: single run; no seeds or confidence intervals stated; GPT-4 extractor validated against volunteers

availability.data: dev public with answers; test answers withheld

prompts.text:
Hint: xxx [optional]
Question: xxx
A. xxx
B. xxx
C. xxx [optional]
D. xxx [optional]
Please select the correct answer from the options above.

You are an AI assistant who will help me to match an answer with several options of a single-choice question. You are provided with a question, several options, and an answer, and you need to find which option is most similar to the answer. If the meaning of all options are significantly different from the answer, output Z. You should only do the matching based exactly on the literal meaning of the options and answer. You should not perform any external inference based on your knowledge during the matching. Your should output a single uppercase character in A, B, C, D (if they are valid options), and Z.

results.claim: GPT-4 matches human choice extraction on hard (heuristic-unparseable) predictions in 91.5% of cases.
results.setup: ~420 samples (10% of VLM outputs that heuristic matching could not parse); extracted choice must equal the human one; best of the LLMs tried
results.quote: GPT-4 achieves the highest level of alignment rate, which is 91.5%

results.claim: Under CircularEval, OpenFlamingo v2 falls from 36.7% (VanillaEval) to 2.6% on MMBench-dev.
results.quote: the performance of OpenFlamingo v2 drops from 36.7% to only 2.6%

results.claim: LLaVA-v1.5-13B beats 7B by 2.1 points under VanillaEval but 4.7 under CircularEval (MMBench-dev).
results.quote: LLaVA-v1.5-13B outperforms its 7B counterpart by 2.1% Top-1 accuracy under VanillaEval, while a much larger performance gap (4.7% Top-1) is observed under CircularEval

results.claim: Top-1 CircularEval accuracy on MMBench-test: InternLM-XComposer2 is best open-source.
Qwen-VL-Max is best proprietary on MMBench-test.
Text-only GPT-4-Turbo scores near random after quality control.
Proprietary VLMs lose about 10% Top-1 moving from VanillaEval to CircularEval (GPT-4v).
GPT-4v rejects answering in 1.8% of CircularEval passes (Gemini-Pro-V 1.6%, Qwen-VL-Max 0.1%); 74% of GPT-4v rejections are celebrity recognition.
results.quote: GPT-4v, Gemini-Pro-V, and Qwen-VL-Max reject answering in 1.8%, 1.6%, and 0.1% of cases across all CircularEval passes in MMBench, respectively

results.claim: Content moderation lowers MMBench-test accuracy by at most 2.4% (upper bound assuming rejected questions answered correctly).
results.quote: the content moderation policy affects the MMBench-test accuracy by up to 2.4%

results.claim: Switching Vicuna 7B to 13B raises overall MMBench-test Top-1 by 8.3% (MiniGPT), 1.5% (InstructBLIP), 3.5% (LLaVA v1.5).
results.quote: MiniGPT, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA v1.5 series outperform their 7B counterparts by 8.3%, 1.5%, and 3.5% overall Top-1 accuracies

results.claim: Exact matching badly underestimates VisualGLM-6B: dev accuracy 19.4 exact vs 36.1 with GPT-4 extractor.
Different LLM choice extractors change dev results little; VisualGLM range ~1.4%, top proprietary at most 0.3%.
results.quote: VisualGLM displays the largest range across all choice extractors, which is around 1.4%

results.claim: VisualGLM-6B heuristic match rate is only 64.8%; LLM extraction adds 23.2 points of dev accuracy.
results.table: Table 1, row VisualGLM-6B, column Match Rate

results.claim: MMBench has 3,217 questions across 20 L-3 abilities; >80% collected from the Internet; dev:test split 4:6.
results.quote: we have gathered a total of 3,217 data samples spanning across 20 distinct L-3 abilities

results.claim: Lowest best-model accuracy L-3 abilities: image quality Amax 61.3%, structuralized image-text 61.5%, physical relation 64.0%, spatial relationship 68.0%.
results.setup: max across all evaluated VLMs, CircularEval

limits: Multiple-choice only; CircularEval makes accuracy much lower than single pass so scores are not comparable across protocols.
Content moderation by proprietary VLMs depresses their scores (up to 2.4%).
Paper is the v5 (MMBench v1.1) revision; earlier versions' numbers differ.
No seeds/variance reported; temperature and max tokens not stated.

terms.definition: each question is fed to a VLM N times (N is the number of choices) with circular shifting of the choices and answer; success only if correct in all passes
